title: Curiosity comes first.
summary: A personal identity for Lay Shah: inventive and discerning, with one unexpected detail that makes a clear impression.

brief.name: Lay Shah
brief.audience: Founders, businesses, and small teams choosing a developer for websites, applications, and practical tools.
brief.direction: Restraint with an unexpected, memorable character.
brief.latitude: Fresh lettering, symbols, and colors are open for exploration. Website typography, colors, and layout are reviewed separately.
brief.ownerWords: At the top, I think it should be curiosity, without which nothing is possible.
brief.interpretation: Explore deeply enough to understand the real need, then explain the choices and value clearly. This is a working creative brief, not a new public tagline.

muse.name: MUBI
muse.alt: Source capture of MUBI’s white wordmark and seven-dot arrangement from its own homepage.
muse.cue: Plain, compact lettering sits beside a small, uneven arrangement of equal-sized dots. The unusual silhouette adds a moment of discovery while the name stays easy to read.
muse.carry: A clear name, an economical shape vocabulary, and one deliberate surprise.
muse.boundary: The dot arrangement, letter shapes, and cinema identity belong to MUBI. Lay’s sketches will explore original forms and ideas.
muse.confirmed: Selected by you: “I would love to go with option C, unexpected character.”

references.name: Josh W. Comeau
references.alt: Source capture of Josh W. Comeau’s colored name, with a tilted W and small caret between the words.
references.observation: A tilted W and a small caret interrupt an otherwise readable name. The surrounding website adds a much more playful illustrated world.
references.lesson: A small, specific change can give lettering a recognizable voice.
references.caution: The whimsical treatment suits his teaching personality. Lay’s clients still need a composed, confident first impression.

references.name: Rauno Freiberg
references.alt: Source capture of Rauno Freiberg’s large black name beside the edge of a yellow circle.
references.observation: The name leads in large, plain lettering. A yellow circle and unusual page composition carry the visual character.
references.lesson: Personality can come from one deliberate interruption around clear typography.
references.caution: This is a name treatment in a larger composition, rather than a standalone graphic symbol. Lay’s finished mark must also hold its own outside the website.

references.name: Paco Coursey
references.alt: Source capture of Paco Coursey’s small, unadorned name on a dark background.
references.observation: A small, unadorned name introduces a restrained, writing-led page. There is no separate graphic logo in this captured heading.
references.lesson: Restraint gives the work and language room to establish credibility.
references.caution: Plain name typography alone offers little visual recognition when removed from its page. Lay needs a more memorable identifying feature.

references.name: Brittany Chiang
references.alt: Source capture of Brittany Chiang’s large pale name and Frontend Engineer label on navy.
references.observation: A large, bold name and a clear role establish an immediate hierarchy against a navy background.
references.lesson: The person’s name can be the clearest anchor in a professional portfolio.
references.caution: Dark backgrounds and neutral sans-serif names recur in this comparison set. Repeating that combination alone would give Lay little distinction.

references.name: Tobias van Schneider / HOVS
references.alt: Source capture of the HOVS serif wordmark in a red tab at the top of Tobias van Schneider’s site.
references.observation: The HOVS wordmark pairs high-contrast serif lettering with an assertive red tab. Tobias’s own products and studio work share the surrounding identity.
references.lesson: A consistent point of view can connect a personal practice and several products.
references.caution: HOVS is a studio identity. Lay Shah remains the primary name here; a new studio name or elaborate badge is outside the brief.

references.name: Bruno Simon
references.alt: Source capture of Bruno Simon’s published square browser icon with a dark diamond and white center.
references.observation: The published browser icon is a simple diamond. The portfolio itself builds recognition through a distinctive interactive driving world.
references.lesson: A logo is one part of a personal identity; demonstrated craft can carry much of its character.
references.caution: An isolated geometric diamond would not give Lay the same distinctive experience. The new mark needs an identifying feature of its own.

findings: Names do much of the identifying work in this set. Josh modifies his lettering; Rauno, Paco, and Brittany largely use their names as typography within a broader composition.
Dark backgrounds and neutral sans-serif lettering recur. They can be well executed, but using them alone would give Lay little visual distinction.
The memorable differences come from particular choices: Josh’s displaced letter, Rauno’s spatial interruption, HOVS’s typographic contrast, and Bruno’s authored experience.
The opportunity for Lay is a composed identity with an identifying detail that survives outside a website. The client should be able to notice that detail before reading its explanation.

criteria.title: Personal relevance
criteria.description: Trace the idea to Lay’s curiosity, understanding, or communication. It should feel plausible for this person and this audience.

criteria.title: Recognizable character
criteria.description: Point to one feature that can be remembered after a brief glance. Keep the name clear and the surprise intentional.

criteria.title: Legibility
criteria.description: Read the name at header size and inspect the compact symbol at actual 16, 24, and 32 pixels. Test pure black and white before color.

criteria.title: Distinction
criteria.description: Compare the visible work against these six identities, MUBI, and the rejected rounds. Record similarities and weaknesses without awarding intent as evidence.

avoid: Reworking the existing LS mark or any of the six rejected concepts.
Copying MUBI’s dots or substituting a familiar tech symbol for a personal idea.
Default curiosity icons such as a magnifying glass, question mark, or eye without a specific original idea.
Using a fashionable font, color effect, or animation as the only source of distinction.
nextStage: Choose two sketch numbers to develop. The next stage refines their lettering and symbols, then compares color and practical applications. No pair has been selected.

concepts.name: Open letter
concepts.idea: The first a opens outward; a quiet detail in a direct, readable name.
concepts.risk: The aperture needs testing at small sizes; the remaining lettering is close to a standard sans.
concepts.construction: Outlined bold humanist lowercase with one opened bowl and tightened optical spacing.
concepts.alt: Lowercase lay shah in bold black lettering, with a small opening cut into the first a.
concepts.caption: An opening in the first a.

concepts.name: Two voices
concepts.idea: A composed first name meets a more conversational, slanted surname.
concepts.risk: Roman-and-italic pairing alone is easy to reproduce; selected lettering would need more authorship.
concepts.construction: Equal-size Newsreader roman and italic outline studies with a custom inter-word interval.
concepts.alt: Lay in upright serif lettering followed by Shah in flowing italic serif, both on one baseline.
concepts.caption: Two registers, one name.

concepts.name: Unrehearsed
concepts.idea: An upright, slightly irregular hand gives the name a candid, approachable voice.
concepts.risk: Its informal tone may undersell complex work; the a/y junctions still need refining.
concepts.construction: Original seven-letter pen construction, open terminals, consistent rounded stroke, no signing flourish.
concepts.alt: Original upright handwritten Lay Shah with irregular rounded letters and a compact y descender.
concepts.caption: Original upright pen lettering.

concepts.name: Margin note
concepts.idea: Lay sits in the quiet space above Shah, like a personal note beside a larger thought.
concepts.risk: The surname dominates and the reading order is unconventional; a header version would need testing.
concepts.construction: Nested two-line serif name, small italic first name in the space above the lower-case surname letters.
concepts.alt: A large serif Shah with a smaller italic Lay nested over the hah, making a compact two-line name.
concepts.caption: A first name in the margin.

concepts.name: Turned page
concepts.idea: One surface turns outwards: exploring something, then making it available to someone else.
concepts.risk: It can read as publishing or education before independent development.
concepts.construction: Asymmetric curved page beside a narrow outward-folded plane; one broad internal crease.
concepts.alt: Two solid black folded-page planes, one curved and one turned outward, with a white crease.
concepts.caption: A page turned towards someone.

concepts.name: Follow-up
concepts.idea: Two deliberately long quotation forms give conversation a strong, compact rhythm.
concepts.risk: Quotation marks are common; this risks looking like a testimonial or messaging product.
concepts.construction: Two solid bowed quotation forms with pointed return tails, offset from a typical quote glyph.
concepts.alt: Two tall custom quotation forms with bowed upper strokes and angular lower tails.
concepts.caption: A conversation, given a shape.

concepts.name: Listening form
concepts.idea: An ear-like silhouette makes attentive listening the identifying gesture.
concepts.risk: It can also read as a lightbulb, or suggest audiology; the association needs your reaction.
concepts.construction: Organic solid outline around one wide carved channel, with an asymmetrical lower lobe.
concepts.alt: A sculpted black ear-like silhouette with one white curved channel and an asymmetric lower lobe.
concepts.caption: Listening, made tangible.

concepts.name: Attentive hare
concepts.idea: A small character with one listening ear introduces warmth and an inquisitive posture.
concepts.risk: Animal identities need repetition to become personal; this may feel too playful for your audience.
concepts.construction: Compact original side-profile hare with one upright ear, one bent ear and two small facial cuts.
concepts.alt: A compact black hare silhouette with one tall ear, one bent ear and a small white eye.
concepts.caption: One ear turns to listen.

concepts.name: The aside
concepts.idea: A folded comma holds a pause beside the name: room to listen before responding.
concepts.risk: Punctuation can feel like an editorial studio; the fold is the detail to make recognizable.
concepts.construction: Broad comma with an angled internal fold, paired with optically spaced upright serif lettering.
concepts.alt: A large black comma with a small triangular white fold, followed by Lay Shah in serif lettering.
concepts.caption: A pause before the response.

concepts.name: Unfold
concepts.idea: Three uneven planes open outwards, suggesting a thought being examined from more than one side.
concepts.risk: Folded forms are common in software identities; this needs a less familiar silhouette if selected.
concepts.construction: Three separate broad planes, one curved edge and unequal fold angles, beside a plain uppercase name.
concepts.alt: Three uneven black folded planes beside uppercase LAY SHAH.
concepts.caption: One thought, opened out.

concepts.name: Inside out
concepts.idea: A broad carved spiral invites a second look at what is happening inside a simple form.
concepts.risk: The spiral can read as a G or a 6 and suggest wellness or audio; it needs a more recognizable silhouette.
concepts.construction: Asymmetric shell-like solid ribbon, one inward turn and an open upper shoulder; restrained lowercase name.
concepts.alt: An irregular black spiral with an open shoulder, paired with lowercase lay shah in sans-serif lettering.
concepts.caption: A second look inside.

concepts.name: Working note
concepts.idea: The name lives on a folded note: a small object associated with thinking things through.
concepts.risk: A document outline is familiar; the asymmetrical fold and lettering would need more refinement.
concepts.construction: Compact folded-note enclosure with a generous square fold and left-aligned two-line name.
concepts.alt: A thin black folded-note outline enclosing Lay above Shah in bold sans-serif lettering.
concepts.caption: A personal working note.

sketchGroups.title: Lettering-led
sketchGroups.description: The name carries the identifying detail.

sketchGroups.title: Symbol-led
sketchGroups.description: A standalone form, before choosing its lettering.

sketchGroups.title: Name + symbol
sketchGroups.description: The relationship between the two carries the idea.

recommendation.reason: 04 gives the full name an unusual, compact arrangement. 09 adds a small characterful device beside a readable name. Developing these would test lettering-led and combined approaches. Neither is selected.
